facts.text: Leganés was founded in 1280 as "Legamar" during Alfonso X's reign and became a Madrid village in 1345.
The Leganés Central railway station opened on 20 June 1876, originally serving the Madrid‑to‑Cáceres line.
The former Santa Isabel Psychiatric Hospital, opened in 1851, was one of Spain's first asylums and now houses part of the Charles III University.
The Polvoranca Hermitage and a Baroque altarpiece by José de Churriguera are key ecclesiastical treasures in Leganés.
Leganés' streets are named after European countries, Latin American nations, and even Don Quixote characters, reflecting a playful naming tradition.
Leganés produced Olympic athletes: cyclist Daniel Yuste in 1968 and taekwondo silver medalists José María Sánchez Élez and José Sanabria in 1988.
